column8: Tue 17 Nov: 3c-3d, the true version of the erase claim: Pacioli (1494, Geijsbeek 1914) answers a wrong ink figure with a counter-entry and both stay on the page, so a top stated early and cut later would show; NUMBERS pointer is section 4 l.453, not l.378, and its four percentages stay in the store (density cut).

Tue 17 Nov: wording guard, kept only with the right attribution: the never cross out or erase line is Manzoni's (Venice, as Geijsbeek 1914 renders his index), never Pacioli's; Manzoni's Italian not read; no CONCEIT line attributes it to Pacioli, so nothing there to fix.

Tue 17 Nov: store only; a charming 1494 precedent for Table 1's identifiers and dates but close to trivia (Book 18) and it serves no decision; never say Pacioli's merchants held government bonds; Taiwan's art. 26 does not bind Laura.

Tue 17 Nov: 2.0 guard evidence: a ledger's ink can hold bad money, so a written figure is not ink; supports the definition's owned, never signed; the synthesis is Q106-035 and the owed against owned point is already Q7c-035.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; a notary's seal attests the book, not the money (Q83 guard); never mix with V2.2's calligraphy seal in 3d, and never ink as a sealed figure.

Tue 17 Nov: struck-but-readable drafts do the job non-photo blue already does in 3c; never print the unrounded $118,072 in prose (density cut: Table 2's note); the later writer behind erasures improper is unconfirmed.

Tue 17 Nov: store; ruling off unused space maps loosely to the cap ($8,476 excess, NUMBERS 4) but the rule stops someone else forging and the space above her top is money she keeps, so trim and bleed in 3c does it better.

Tue 17 Nov: a yearly account to co-sponsors is a new process outside the IPS, and before 2031 it would state figures the plan states only at the 2031 meetings (SKELETON 3c, IPS l.15); the proverb is decoration.
Tue 17 Nov: store; a 1494 precedent for 3e's custody clause (checked each January against the broker statement, already in SKELETON); never the broker's record is the ink.

Tue 17 Nov: 3d store; Taiwan's Accounting Act art. 67 (no patching, rubbing or scraping) is the national version of Q83's turn but lacks the word pencil and is about the record, not ownership; Q83-029 stays the turn; never legal advice.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q106-010 for company books (two red lines, signed); one Taiwan correction rule is enough, and red adds a colour the conceit avoids.
Tue 17 Nov: guard only for Q106-011: quote the Chinese with Keel's translation, never the 2021 official English of art. 13.
Tue 17 Nov: wording guard: never say Taiwan's Business Entity Accounting Act forbids erasing; if named, it forbids altering or destroying the books (arts 24, 71, 76).

Tue 17 Nov: 3d store; no figure in the books without a real event behind it is a neat Taiwan echo of no stated figure without an owned Treasury, but it binds companies, not a donor's letter; Q67-043 and Q43-009 carry the point more directly.
Tue 17 Nov: store; the parallel is the word 確定 only; 3c's certain keeps the stated range as its subject (Q71, Q74), never the figures.

Tue 17 Nov: 3c outside check, verified quotes, but IAS 37's bar is virtually certain, a likelihood, while Laura's is owned, which is stricter; never Laura's rule is IAS 37's rule or IFRS requires, never set it beside KPMG's probability is not a factor (US GAAP), never prudence or conservatism (CONCEIT 5b rank 1).

Tue 17 Nov: 3b-3d: IAS 37 would disclose a probable gain and Laura offers none of her flexibility ($21,347, NUMBERS 4), backing never offered; the change happens on one date, the move in January 2031; a parallel, never a rule she follows.

Tue 17 Nov: 3d test from US GAAP (FAS 5 para 17, ASC 450-30): Laura's words must avoid misleading implications as to the likelihood of realization, so nothing in them suggests more than the stated top; fits SKELETON 3d's no up to, no at least.

Tue 17 Nov: 3c's best outside answer to why not state a top early: for gains probability is not a factor (KPMG on ASC 450-30); fix: 97% is Keel arithmetic on NUMBERS 4 l.453's 2.9% (not l.378) and is said as aha row 7 words it; drop the treats losses early clause, which reads as conservatism (CONCEIT 5b rank 1).

Tue 17 Nov: the VT mapping likely breaks: Concepts Statement 5 para 83, which Deloitte cites, counts fungible units with quoted prices in an active market as readily convertible (check at source), so VT would be realizable; split ink from pencil by payer and date, never by convertibility; never fixed for IBTM's payout.

Tue 17 Nov: keep the guard (3c says certain, never virtually certain) but drop which the top passes only after the move and not a percentage: IAS 37 leaves the bar unquantified, so where the top crosses it is Keel's inference.

Tue 17 Nov: 3d candidate, Taiwan's own law fixes the amount line (票據法 art. 11, Taichung ruling 23 Mar 2026), but a note is owed, so use it only for writing the amount once, in the team's sentence, never as what makes a figure ink (owned, never signed, Q42); one Taiwan turn with Q83-029; read the statute on the MOJ page; never legal advice.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; about vouchers inside government, and no source says any co-sponsor applies it; never imply co-sponsors check Laura's figures this way.

Tue 17 Nov: the link between the grant rules and art. 67 is Keel's reading; say the same words, never derived from, and drop not a local quirk, which implies the link; never co-sponsors count only ink.

Tue 17 Nov: 2.0 or 3c, pairs with Q106-026: bookkeepers really kept entries in ink and running totals in pencil, a literal pencil and ink in the judge's own trade; close to finance (Q58 claim 4), so one clause; never in Table 1.

Tue 17 Nov: 3c-3b, the strongest new turn that keeps the mapping: a pencil total was inked only when the account was ruled and closed, as the top is owned only at the move, while half the account stays open as her flexibility, the pencil never inked; needs no glossary; textbook authors not recorded.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e, a glossary-free alternative to registration marks (panel 3) but a coloured-pencil tick gives pencil a second meaning beside the definition; say a tick beside each owned line, never a pencil tick or a colour; Castenholz read only via Ariail and Hughes.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q106-027 (ticking each figure to its voucher); the CUSIP tie is already Table 1's job (Q38).

Tue 17 Nov: store; Peloubet's ink is an impression of authenticity, so the parallel breaks under its own disanalogy; useful only as the warning that an inked look without an owned Treasury is the fault the conceit avoids.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; the two reasons are exits for when the plan cannot be carried out (Q7b-033), not marks on corrections; author and year unverified.

Tue 17 Nov: beside the 2.0 definition a cheque teaches inked as signed and owed, which V2.1 and Q42 rule out (ink is defined with owned); cheques correct in the open but that is record integrity, not the conceit's rule.
Tue 17 Nov: in the red rests on secondary pages; the guard (no in the red or in the black, no colour for VT) is covered by Q106-033 and CONCEIT's no-puns, no-colour rules.
Tue 17 Nov: guard only: red ink marked closings, gains and corrections, not loss alone; the report uses no colour words.

Tue 17 Nov: 3c-3d, a witty glossary-free turn (the inker may paint a mistake out, the bookkeeper may not hide one) but fix: the will be construed as deceit quote is Manzoni's as Geijsbeek renders him, never Pacioli's; and it must not undo V2.2 3d's printed page (use one frame for co-sponsors, never lives in a ledger, not on a comic page).

Tue 17 Nov: guard for every ledger turn (V2.4 guards 1 and 7): borrow the ledger's visibility, never its recorded for owned; ledger ink records the past and can hold bad money, Laura's ink is a Treasury held to its date (IPS l.13).
Tue 17 Nov: store only; the parallel breaks under its own disanalogy, since all three of Pacioli's books are in ink and record past trades, not forecasts.
